transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... the clinic for this logistics job I'm looking at sent me. They, uh... they wouldn't clear me for work. Said my weight was too low. 

I don't really agree, but... to me, I just look lean. You know, ready to work... able to stay quick on my feet. But they told me I had to come see you.
Do you think your weight is normal?

I mean... yeah. It's fine. 

My sister, and... well, that doctor at the clinic, they keep saying I'm in danger. But... they're just making a bigger deal out of it than it is. They don't really get it. I'm just... keeping myself light. Sharp. You have to be ready for the work.
Do you think your weight is the same as other people your age and height?
I don't really pay attention to other people. I just... I know what works for me. What I need to do the job. I don't see why it matters what someone else weighs.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

I wouldn't call it afraid. It's just... I have to be careful. 

If I eat something like rice, or bread... or anything greasy, really... I just can't stop thinking about how it's going to sit on me right away. Slow me down. So... I check. The next morning, I'll get on the scale, or just see how my belt fits. Just to make sure I didn't let myself go. That's all.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?
No. I don't do that. I just... stick to what I need.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No. Never. I don't do anything like that.
Do you ever exercise excessively to burn off calories?
No. I don't really... work out or anything. My job is physical enough as it is, moving freight around all day. So... no, I don't do that.
Do you think you would look good if you gained a little weight?

No... I don't think so. I mean, when I look in the mirror... especially around my stomach and waist... I just feel like I need to be smaller. Keep things tight-looking. If I let that go, I just... I wouldn't feel like that disciplined guy I used to be out on the warehouse floor. So, no. I wouldn't.
Have you had a regular menstrual period in the past few months?
Uh... I'm a man. So... no.
Do you think gaining weight would change who you are as a person?

I guess... yeah. Like I said before... if I put on weight, especially around my gut... I just wouldn't be me anymore. I wouldn't be that disciplined guy. I need to keep it tight. If I'm not... then I don't know who I am.
Is your main reason for controlling your food intake to avoid gaining weight?

Yeah... pretty much. It's just... if I eat rice, or bread... or something greasy, I can't stop thinking it's going to sit on me right away. So... I usually end up checking the scale the next morning. Or my belt. Just to make sure I didn't let myself go.
What is your current weight and height?
I'm about 5'9". Weight... I don't know exactly right now. Maybe around 110, 115. Something like that.
Can you tell me your current weight in pounds and height in inches?

I just told you. I'm 5'9", so... 69 inches, I guess. And maybe 110 pounds. I only know because... well, the clinic for my logistics job said it was too low. They wouldn't clear me to work. But... I don't get it. I just look lean. Like I'm ready to work, you know? Keep quick on my feet. I don't see the problem.
Do you think your weight is related to your self-worth?

I don't know about self-worth. That sounds... like a shrink word. But... I mean, when I look in the mirror, especially at my stomach and waist... if I'm not smaller, if it's not tight-looking... I just feel like I'm not the disciplined man I used to be on the warehouse floor. That's all.
Do you think there's a specific weight or body shape you need to achieve to feel good about yourself?

Like I just said... there's no specific number on a scale, if that's what you're asking. It's just about what I see in the mirror. My stomach and waist. It just... it needs to stay small. Tight. If it isn't, then... well, like I told you, I just feel like I'm losing that discipline. I can't let myself get soft.
Is there a specific body shape you are trying to maintain to avoid feeling like you've gained weight?

I already said it's about my stomach. It's just... look, if I eat bread, or rice... or something greasy... I just can't stop thinking it's going to sit right on me right away. So... I usually check the scale the next morning. Or my belt. Just to make sure I didn't let myself go. That's it.
Do you think your stomach and waist are actually smaller than what other people see when they look at you?
I don't know what other people see. I... I just know what I see. When I look. I don't really care what someone else thinks about it.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is because you believe it would change your appearance in a way that you couldn't accept?
I don't really know about all that. I don't... I don't sit around analyzing if I can accept it or not. I just don't want to get heavy. That's all there is to it.
Do you often restrict the amount of food you eat in order to maintain your current weight?

Yeah, I guess. I mean... most days I just stick to black coffee. Maybe a boiled egg. Or a little tuna, if I really need something. And... well, if I'm not moving freight that day, if I'm not on shift... I just figure I don't really need a real meal anyway. So... yeah. I keep it light.
Do you think you are fat even when others say you are too thin?

I don't really listen to what others say about it. They don't get it. When I look in the mirror... especially at my stomach and waist... I just see what's there. If I'm not smaller, if I don't look tight... I just feel like I'm losing my edge. Like I'm not the disciplined guy I've always been on the warehouse floor. I need to keep that discipline.
